title: The mark a crow leaves behind
question: When a crow eats a plant, the square it leaves looks exactly like a row that was hoed and never sown — so the game marks it. The mark it draws today is three small clods of earth, scattered across the square and rising one after another on a slow loop. On 15 September you looked at your daughter's farm, saw them, and asked what they were and whether they were a bug. That is the mark failing at the only job it has. What should a raided square look like instead? Recommendation: a feather.
why_now: The mark was always a placeholder. It is made of pixels the game already ships — three patches lifted out of the dirt sheet — because a first version is allowed to be, and the code itself says a drawn version is the artist's to do. This is that moment arriving, and it arrived the way these things should: somebody looked at the game and could not read it. Her farm has two raided squares on it right now, so whatever wins can be judged on a real farm rather than a mock-up.

options.label: A feather
options.detail: One small feather left lying on the square. It is the only object that says 'a bird was here' without a word, it needs no explaining to a four-year-old, and it belongs to the vocabulary the crow night already built. One sprite to draw. The risk is that a feather on bare soil is quiet, and quiet is what went wrong last time.

options.label: The stripped plant
options.detail: Leave a bitten stalk where the crop was, instead of clearing the square to bare earth. The loss reads as a loss rather than as ground, and it says which plant was taken. More art — a stripped stage per crop — and it changes what the square looks like she has to clear before replanting.

options.label: Keep the clods, but sit them down and darken them
options.detail: The cheapest fix: stop them floating, make them a clear step darker than the soil. Costs almost nothing and keeps everything else. It is also the least likely to work — the problem is not that the clods are hard to see, it is that earth on earth does not say 'crow'.

options.label: Say it once at the sleep instead
options.detail: Leave the square alone and name the raid on the Day-N card the next morning: a bird took one. The news arrives once, in words or a picture, and the field stays clean. The cost is that by the time she is standing on the square there is nothing to connect it to what she was told.
